# Bombadil Property-Based UI Testing — Spike Handoff

**Date:** 2026-07-26
**Status:** 🟡 Researched and scoped; prerequisites landed; **nothing Bombadil-specific built yet.**
The demo-seed local-only migration that unblocks it is done and verified. The
remaining work is the dev auto-login and the specification file — see
[Remaining work](#remaining-work).

## The question

Can we run [Bombadil](https://github.com/antithesishq/bombadil) — Antithesis's
property-based testing tool for web UIs — against **only** the local stack, scoped
to a **single page**, with **no receipts reaching Mistral**?

**Answer: yes.** All three constraints are satisfiable. Two of them are not
satisfiable through Bombadil's own configuration, which is the main thing this
document exists to record.

## Use the browser driver, not the terminal one

The spike started from the wrong manual. Bombadil ships two independent drivers:

| Driver       | Docs                                                        | Drives                       |
| ------------ | ----------------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------- |
| **browser**  | <https://antithesishq.github.io/bombadil/browser/1-introduction.html> | Anything using the DOM       |
| terminal     | <https://antithesishq.github.io/bombadil/terminal/1-introduction.html> | TUIs over stdin/a text grid  |

We want **browser**. The terminal manual is a different tool for a different job
and nothing in it transfers.

Useful pages: [specification language](https://antithesishq.github.io/bombadil/browser/3-specification-language.html),
[CLI reference](https://antithesishq.github.io/bombadil/browser/4-reference.html).

## How it works

A loop: extract DOM state → check every property → choose and perform an action →
wait for an event (navigation, DOM mutation, or timeout) → repeat. You supply
properties and action generators as a TypeScript ES module; Bombadil drives the
exploration.

**Four properties come free with no specification at all**: uncaught exceptions,
unhandled promise rejections, error-level console logs, and HTTP 4xx/5xx
responses. Pointing it at a URL with no spec file is a genuinely useful first run.

Specification vocabulary: `extract(state => …)` returns a `Cell<T>` read via
`.current`; formulas are built with `always` / `eventually` / `next` / `now`,
combined with `.and()` / `.or()` / `.implies()` / `.not()`, and time-bounded with
`.within(5, "seconds")`. Action generators are `actions(() => [...])` returning a
weighted tree, with `weighted([[10, a], [1, b]])` to bias exploration. Defaults
live at `@antithesishq/bombadil/browser/defaults`.

Version at time of writing: **v0.6.1**, published 2026-06-18 — comfortably clear of
our `.npmrc` `min-release-age=7`. Exit codes: `0` normal, `1` error, `2` property
violation.

## Three findings that shape the design

### 1. `<ORIGIN>` cannot scope to a single page

The CLI argument is documented as _"Starting URL of the test (also used as a
boundary so that Bombadil doesn't navigate to other websites)"_ — the boundary is
**origin-level**, i.e. `http://localhost:5173`. Passing
`http://localhost:5173/transactions` will **not** stop it wandering into
`/expenses`, `/receipts` or `/profile`.

Single-page confinement therefore has to come from the specification:

- Do **not** `export * from "@antithesishq/bombadil/browser/defaults"` — the defaults
  include general navigation and click-any-semantic-element generators. Re-export
  the default _properties_ only, and hand-write the action generator.
- Add a tripwire property (`always(() => location.pathname === "/transactions")`)
  so an escape is a loud violation rather than silent scope creep.

### 2. There is no network interception, blocking, or mocking

Nothing in the CLI or the specification language stubs outbound requests. Keeping
receipts away from Mistral is an application-level concern, and fortunately a
narrow one: the browser's **only** Mistral touchpoint is
`src/lib/services/ReceiptService.ts:31` → `POST /api/ocr/extract`. A page that
never uploads a receipt never reaches it.

Belt and braces: run the dev server with **no `MISTRAL_API_KEY`**. It is a dynamic
import (see the comment in `playwright.config.ts`), so the endpoint fails at
request time rather than build time — which turns the free "no 5xx responses"
property into a tripwire. If Bombadil ever finds a path to OCR, we get a
violation instead of a silent API bill.

### 3. There is no authentication support

No `--storage-state`, no cookie flag, no login helper. `--header` injects HTTP
headers only, which is useless here: `src/lib/supabaseClient.ts` uses plain
`createClient` with `persistSession: true`, so the session lives in
**localStorage**.

Two ways out, and we chose the second:

- **`bombadil browser test-external --remote-debugger http://localhost:9222`** —
  launch your own Chromium, log in by hand, attach Bombadil to the live tab.
  Rejected: it depends on `--create-target=false` attaching to the _existing_
  authenticated tab, which the docs do not confirm, and it needs manual
  choreography before every run.
- **A dev-only auto-login** ✅ — establish a real Supabase session at boot. Auth
  stays fully intact, plain `bombadil browser test` works, and the run is
  reproducible from one command.

Note this deliberately means Bombadil never explores the logged-out state or the
login page. Acceptable given the single-page scope; revisit if the scope widens.

## Why not a true auth bypass

Considered and rejected. Every protected page independently calls
`supabase.auth.getSession()`, and all reads are RLS-gated on `family_members`.
Without a session the pages render "No family found…" and Bombadil would spend its
whole budget exploring an empty shell. Worse, it would mean adding a no-session
code path that exists only for the test tool — the opposite of the point.

## Target page: `/transactions`

`src/routes/transactions/+page.svelte` (588 lines) has the richest client-side
state that never touches receipt upload: date/vendor/amount/card-type filters, a
temp-vs-applied filter split, URL-param sync via `$effect`, the `includeIgnored`
toggle, row selection, and client-side sorting in `DataTable`.

Candidate properties: filtered rows are always a subset of all rows; clearing
filters restores the full count; the URL params and the filter panel never
disagree.

**Hazard:** the page has Delete and bulk-delete. A run _will_ destroy seeded data,
so expect to re-seed between runs. `/spending` is read-only and safer but has far
less state worth exploring.

**Hazard:** the header renders a Logout button whenever `$session` is set. If
Bombadil clicks it the session is gone and the rest of the run explores `/login`.
Exclude the header from the action generator. Do **not** auto-re-login on
`SIGNED_OUT` — that would mask genuine session-loss bugs.

## Prerequisites — done

Demo data is now local-only, which is what gives the auto-login a stable
credential. Completed and verified 2026-07-26:

- Demo family torn down in production; verified by direct SQL (demo users, demo
  family, and orphan sweeps across every family/user-scoped table plus
  `storage.objects` — all zero).
- `readConfig()` hard-fails on any non-loopback `PUBLIC_SUPABASE_URL`, before the
  service-role client is built.
- Demo password is now the checked-in constant `DEMO_PASSWORD` in
  `scripts/demo/common.ts` (`DemoFamily-2026!local`), verified to authenticate
  against the local stack.
- Script names simplified — `npm run dev` and `npm run seed:demo` are the local
  ones; production is the explicit `npm run dev:remote`.
- `npm run check` now type-checks `scripts/` and `e2e/`, which it never did before.

See [Demo data seed](../demo-seed.md) and [Local development](../local-dev.md).

## Remaining work

1. **`src/lib/dev/autoLogin.ts` + hook in `src/routes/+layout.svelte:28`.**
   Must complete _before_ `authChecked = true`, or the layout briefly treats the
   user as logged out and the run starts with a redirect flap.

   Gate on **`import.meta.env.DEV` AND a loopback `PUBLIC_SUPABASE_URL`** — both,
   for different reasons. `import.meta.env.DEV` is what gets the credential
   dead-code-eliminated from the production bundle (a runtime check alone would
   still ship the password string). The loopback check is what stops plain
   `npm run dev`… — which is now local, but `dev:remote` is still DEV — from firing
   demo credentials at production.

   `npm run test:e2e` is unaffected: it runs `vite build && vite preview`, so DEV
   is false and the auto-login is not in that bundle.

2. **`npm run db:fresh`** = `db:reset && seed:demo`. Reset-to-known-state matters
   more here than in normal dev: `--reproduce` only replays faithfully from an
   identical starting state, and the docs are explicit that reproductions fail when
   "application state has changed".

3. **The specification** — `bombadil/transactions.ts`. Default properties only (no
   `export *`), a hand-written action generator confined to the page's own
   controls, the pathname tripwire, and the filter/sort properties above.

4. **Decide where it runs.** Local-only for now. A GitHub Action exists
   (`antithesishq/bombadil-action@v2`) if we later want nightly runs.

## Suggested first run

Deliberately with **no specification file** — just to confirm the binary installs
and the free properties report before investing in a spec:

```bash
npm run db:up
npm run seed:demo
npm run dev                    # localhost:5173, no MISTRAL_API_KEY
npx bombadil browser test --time-limit 2m --output-path bombadil-out \
  http://localhost:5173/login
npx bombadil browser inspect bombadil-out   # timeline UI, violation markers
```

Then repeat against `/transactions` once auto-login lands, adding the spec file as
the final argument.

## Ruled out — do not redo

- **The terminal driver.** Wrong tool; it drives TUIs.
- **Scoping to one page via `<ORIGIN>`.** Origin-level only; must be done in the spec.
- **Network mocking to block Mistral.** Bombadil has no such feature.
- **`--header` for authentication.** The session is in localStorage, not a header.
- **A true auth/RLS bypass.** Yields an empty shell and a test-only code path.
- **`test-external` + remote debugger.** Viable fallback, but unverified and manual;
  superseded by auto-login.
- **Re-logging-in on `SIGNED_OUT`.** Masks real session-loss bugs.

## Open questions

- Does `--create-target=false` attach to an existing authenticated tab? Unresolved —
  only matters if we fall back to `test-external`.
- No documented `--seed` flag for the browser driver, despite the terminal driver
  having one. Reproduction is via `--reproduce <TRACE>` instead. Worth re-checking

31	## Engineering
32	
33	- **✅ DONE — unauthenticated data-forgery chain closed.** The [Security Remediation PRD](prd-done/prd-security-remediation.md) shipped R2–R5 in `20260717_security_remediation_chain.sql` (+ follow-up `20260718_fix_f3_revoke_anon.sql`) and **verified all five §Verification checks against the live deployment on 2026-07-17**: anon `find_user_by_email` (R4/H1) and `insert_receipt_with_context` (R2/C2) denied, `family_members` reads scoped via an `is_member_of()` SECURITY DEFINER helper (R5/H2), tautological receipts INSERT/UPDATE `WITH CHECK` fixed to `fm.family_id = receipts.family_id` (R3/C3), and webhook signature enforced (R1/C1). Verified with the throwaway `.scratch/verify-security.sh` (uncommitted). PRD moved to `docs/prd-done/`.
34	- **✅ DONE — family_members self-join closed.** The open `"Users can insert their own membership"` INSERT policy (which, with the `USING(true)` SELECT, let any authed user self-join any family for a whole-tenant breach) was **dropped** in `20260717_security_remediation_chain.sql`. There is now no client membership-write path — legitimate membership goes through the `SECURITY DEFINER` `ensure_default_family()` (bypasses RLS). Verified live 2026-07-17 (self-insert into an arbitrary family rejected). The sanctioned invite-based replacement is designed in [PRD — Family Invitations](prd-family-invitations.md).
35	- **🟠 HIGH SECURITY — unverified, non-unique profile emails allow email-ingestion hijack.** _(Found 2026-07-17 audit.)_ The add-email flow (`src/routes/profile/+page.svelte`) lets a user attach ANY address to their profile (`profiles.email_1..5`) with only format + within-own-profile dedup — **no ownership verification and no cross-user unique constraint** (`002_profiles_table.sql`). The Resend webhook attributes inbound receipts via `find_user_by_email(sender)`, which falls through to those profile columns (`resend/handler.ts`). So an attacker can claim a victim's forwarding/secondary address and have the victim's forwarded receipts ingested into the attacker's account (data leak), or make attribution nondeterministic (`limit 1`) when two profiles claim the same address, or pre-claim an address to poison a future user. Not closed by the webhook-signature fix (abuse is by a legit authed user). Fix: confirm ownership via emailed token before an alias participates in lookup; add a global `UNIQUE(lower(email))` (ideally a normalized `profile_emails` table); prefer exact `auth.users` identity over unverified aliases.
36	- **✅ DONE — anon-executable seed functions locked down.** `create_default_hierarchy` / `create_default_categories` carried a **direct** `anon` EXECUTE grant (Supabase default privileges), so `anon` could seed rows into empty tenants. `20260717_security_remediation_chain.sql` revoked `FROM PUBLIC`, but live testing showed that missed the direct anon grant (the call still executed, blocked only by a FK) — so `20260718_fix_f3_revoke_anon.sql` added explicit `REVOKE … FROM anon`; `authenticated` keeps its grant (the `CategoryService` caller). Verified live 2026-07-17. **Lesson learned:** on Supabase, `REVOKE … FROM PUBLIC` alone does NOT remove `anon`/`authenticated` — they hold _direct_ grants via default privileges, so revoke those roles explicitly. (Still open: a sweep of any _other_ `SECURITY DEFINER` functions for the same missing REVOKE.)

1	# Bombadil Property-Based UI Testing — Spike Handoff
2	
3	**Date:** 2026-07-26
4	**Status:** 🟡 Researched and scoped; prerequisites landed; **nothing Bombadil-specific built yet.**
5	The demo-seed local-only migration that unblocks it is done and verified. The
6	remaining work is the dev auto-login and the specification file — see
7	[Remaining work](#remaining-work).
8	
9	## The question
10	
11	Can we run [Bombadil](https://github.com/antithesishq/bombadil) — Antithesis's
12	property-based testing tool for web UIs — against **only** the local stack, scoped
13	to a **single page**, with **no receipts reaching Mistral**?
14	
15	**Answer: yes.** All three constraints are satisfiable. Two of them are not
16	satisfiable through Bombadil's own configuration, which is the main thing this
17	document exists to record.
18	
19	## Use the browser driver, not the terminal one
20	
21	The spike started from the wrong manual. Bombadil ships two independent drivers:
22	
23	| Driver      | Docs                                                                   | Drives                      |
24	| ----------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------- |
25	| **browser** | <https://antithesishq.github.io/bombadil/browser/1-introduction.html>  | Anything using the DOM      |
26	| terminal    | <https://antithesishq.github.io/bombadil/terminal/1-introduction.html> | TUIs over stdin/a text grid |
27	
28	We want **browser**. The terminal manual is a different tool for a different job
29	and nothing in it transfers.
30	
31	Useful pages: [specification language](https://antithesishq.github.io/bombadil/browser/3-specification-language.html),
32	[CLI reference](https://antithesishq.github.io/bombadil/browser/4-reference.html).
33	
34	## How it works
35	
36	A loop: extract DOM state → check every property → choose and perform an action →
37	wait for an event (navigation, DOM mutation, or timeout) → repeat. You supply
38	properties and action generators as a TypeScript ES module; Bombadil drives the
39	exploration.
40	
41	**Four properties come free with no specification at all**: uncaught exceptions,
42	unhandled promise rejections, error-level console logs, and HTTP 4xx/5xx
43	responses. Pointing it at a URL with no spec file is a genuinely useful first run.
44	
45	Specification vocabulary: `extract(state => …)` returns a `Cell<T>` read via
46	`.current`; formulas are built with `always` / `eventually` / `next` / `now`,
47	combined with `.and()` / `.or()` / `.implies()` / `.not()`, and time-bounded with
48	`.within(5, "seconds")`. Action generators are `actions(() => [...])` returning a
49	weighted tree, with `weighted([[10, a], [1, b]])` to bias exploration. Defaults
50	live at `@antithesishq/bombadil/browser/defaults`.
51	
52	Version at time of writing: **v0.6.1**, published 2026-06-18 — comfortably clear of
53	our `.npmrc` `min-release-age=7`. Exit codes: `0` normal, `1` error, `2` property
54	violation.
55	
56	## Three findings that shape the design
57	
58	### 1. `<ORIGIN>` cannot scope to a single page
59	
60	The CLI argument is documented as _"Starting URL of the test (also used as a
61	boundary so that Bombadil doesn't navigate to other websites)"_ — the boundary is
62	**origin-level**, i.e. `http://localhost:5173`. Passing
63	`http://localhost:5173/transactions` will **not** stop it wandering into
64	`/expenses`, `/receipts` or `/profile`.
65	
66	Single-page confinement therefore has to come from the specification:
67	
68	- Do **not** `export * from "@antithesishq/bombadil/browser/defaults"` — the defaults
69	  include general navigation and click-any-semantic-element generators. Re-export
70	  the default _properties_ only, and hand-write the action generator.
71	- Add a tripwire property (`always(() => location.pathname === "/transactions")`)
72	  so an escape is a loud violation rather than silent scope creep.
73	
74	### 2. There is no network interception, blocking, or mocking
75	
76	Nothing in the CLI or the specification language stubs outbound requests. Keeping
77	receipts away from Mistral is an application-level concern, and fortunately a
78	narrow one: the browser's **only** Mistral touchpoint is
79	`src/lib/services/ReceiptService.ts:31` → `POST /api/ocr/extract`. A page that
80	never uploads a receipt never reaches it.
81	
82	Belt and braces: run the dev server with **no `MISTRAL_API_KEY`**. It is a dynamic
83	import (see the comment in `playwright.config.ts`), so the endpoint fails at
84	request time rather than build time — which turns the free "no 5xx responses"
85	property into a tripwire. If Bombadil ever finds a path to OCR, we get a
86	violation instead of a silent API bill.
87	
88	### 3. There is no authentication support
89	
90	No `--storage-state`, no cookie flag, no login helper. `--header` injects HTTP
91	headers only, which is useless here: `src/lib/supabaseClient.ts` uses plain
92	`createClient` with `persistSession: true`, so the session lives in
93	**localStorage**.
94	
95	Two ways out, and we chose the second:
96	
97	- **`bombadil browser test-external --remote-debugger http://localhost:9222`** —
98	  launch your own Chromium, log in by hand, attach Bombadil to the live tab.
99	  Rejected: it depends on `--create-target=false` attaching to the _existing_
100	  authenticated tab, which the docs do not confirm, and it needs manual
101	  choreography before every run.
102	- **A dev-only auto-login** ✅ — establish a real Supabase session at boot. Auth
103	  stays fully intact, plain `bombadil browser test` works, and the run is
104	  reproducible from one command.
105	
106	Note this deliberately means Bombadil never explores the logged-out state or the
107	login page. Acceptable given the single-page scope; revisit if the scope widens.
108	
109	## Why not a true auth bypass
110	
111	Considered and rejected. Every protected page independently calls
112	`supabase.auth.getSession()`, and all reads are RLS-gated on `family_members`.
113	Without a session the pages render "No family found…" and Bombadil would spend its
114	whole budget exploring an empty shell. Worse, it would mean adding a no-session
115	code path that exists only for the test tool — the opposite of the point.
116	
117	## Target page: `/transactions`
118	
119	`src/routes/transactions/+page.svelte` (588 lines) has the richest client-side
120	state that never touches receipt upload: date/vendor/amount/card-type filters, a
121	temp-vs-applied filter split, URL-param sync via `$effect`, the `includeIgnored`
122	toggle, row selection, and client-side sorting in `DataTable`.
123	
124	Candidate properties: filtered rows are always a subset of all rows; clearing
125	filters restores the full count; the URL params and the filter panel never
126	disagree.
127	
128	**Hazard:** the page has Delete and bulk-delete. A run _will_ destroy seeded data,
129	so expect to re-seed between runs. `/spending` is read-only and safer but has far
130	less state worth exploring.
131	
132	**Hazard:** the header renders a Logout button whenever `$session` is set. If
133	Bombadil clicks it the session is gone and the rest of the run explores `/login`.
134	Exclude the header from the action generator. Do **not** auto-re-login on
135	`SIGNED_OUT` — that would mask genuine session-loss bugs.
136	
137	## Prerequisites — done
138	
139	Demo data is now local-only, which is what gives the auto-login a stable
140	credential. Completed and verified 2026-07-26:
141	
142	- Demo family torn down in production; verified by direct SQL (demo users, demo
143	  family, and orphan sweeps across every family/user-scoped table plus
144	  `storage.objects` — all zero).
145	- `readConfig()` hard-fails on any non-loopback `PUBLIC_SUPABASE_URL`, before the
146	  service-role client is built.
147	- Demo password is now the checked-in constant `DEMO_PASSWORD` in
148	  `scripts/demo/common.ts` (`DemoFamily-2026!local`), verified to authenticate
149	  against the local stack.
150	- Script names simplified — `npm run dev` and `npm run seed:demo` are the local
151	  ones; production is the explicit `npm run dev:remote`.

Written and the gate is green.

## `docs/plans/2026-07-26-bombadil-property-testing-spike.md`

Structured so the next person (or future us) doesn't repeat the dead ends:

- **The question and the verdict** — yes, all three constraints are satisfiable, but two of them *not* through Bombadil's own configuration. That's the headline the doc exists to preserve.
- **The wrong-manual correction** — a table pointing at the browser driver vs the terminal one, since that's how the spike started and it cost real time.
- **How it works + the spec vocabulary** — enough to write the first property without re-reading the manual: `extract`/`Cell.current`, the temporal operators, `.within()`, `actions()`, `weighted()`, exit codes, and v0.6.1's publish date against our `min-release-age` rule.
- **Three findings that shape the design** — `<ORIGIN>` is origin-level not path-level (quoted verbatim); no network mocking; no auth support. Each paired with the workaround.
- **Why not a true auth bypass** — recorded as a rejected option with the reasoning, since it's the obvious idea someone will re-propose.
- **Target page and its two hazards** — the delete buttons and the Logout trapdoor.
- **Prerequisites (done) vs remaining work** — with the DEV-*and*-loopback gate spelled out, including why each half is load-bearing.
- **Suggested first run** — deliberately spec-less, to prove the binary works before investing in a spec.
- **"Ruled out — do not redo"** — seven dead ends in one list.
- **Open questions** — the unresolved `--create-target` semantics, the missing `--seed` flag on the browser driver, and the possibility upstream adds auth and makes the auto-login moot.

I also added a `🟡 in progress` pointer in the backlog's Engineering section, per the convention that `product-backlog.md` is the single working list.

One thing to flag: the doc states `npm run test:e2e` is unaffected by the planned auto-login because it builds with `vite build && vite preview` (DEV false). That's reasoned from `playwright.config.ts`, not yet demonstrated — it becomes a real claim to verify when the auto-login actually lands.

It is installed — at `~/.claude/skills/handoff/SKILL.md`. Two things stacked up so neither invocation path fired.

## 1. It's deliberately hidden from me

Its frontmatter sets:

```yaml
disable-model-invocation: true
```

That flag excludes a skill from the available-skills list I'm given, so I can't select it via the Skill tool. It's user-invocable only, by design.

The correlation across your skills is exact — 13 hidden, 10 visible, no exceptions:

| Visible to me (`false`) | Hidden (`true`) |
|---|---|
| codebase-design, diagnosing-bugs, domain-modeling, find-skills, grilling, prototype, research, seo-optimizer, systems-thinking, tdd | ask-matt, grill-me, grill-with-docs, **handoff**, implement, improve-codebase-architecture, setup-matt-pocock-skills, teach, to-spec, to-tickets, triage, wayfinder, writing-great-skills |

## 2. The CLI didn't expand it either

Slash commands only expand when the message *starts* with them. You wrote "write a **/handoff** for the bombadil portion…" — mid-sentence, so it arrived as plain prose. Had it been the first token, the CLI would have injected the skill's instructions and the `disable-model-invocation` flag wouldn't have mattered.

So: the flag blocked my path, the phrasing blocked yours.

## This matters — the skill would have produced something different

Now that I can read it, its instructions diverge from what I built in three ways:

- **Location:** save to `tmp/` at the workspace root, explicitly *not* the OS temp dir. I wrote to `docs/plans/`.
- **A "suggested skills" section** listing which skills the next agent should invoke. Mine has none.
- **Don't duplicate content already captured in other artifacts** — reference them by path instead. Mine deliberately restates the Bombadil findings in full, on the theory that a durable repo doc should stand alone.
- **Redact sensitive information, such as passwords.** Mine includes `DemoFamily-2026!local` verbatim. That's a deliberately checked-in local-only constant already in `scripts/demo/common.ts` and echoed by the seed, so it isn't a leak — but the skill would have stripped it.

Those are different artifacts for different purposes: a transient session handoff versus a permanent design record. Mine is the latter.

To get the real thing, start a message with `/handoff` as the first token. Happy to keep the `docs/plans/` doc alongside it, or delete it if you'd rather have just the one — say which.
